newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up on slow day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up on slow day.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds posted about 1/8 point gain on a quiet Election Day eve.
"It is the lull before election," a trader said.
High grade bonds were up a touch, while dollar bonds ended up 1/8 on the day. The secondary market was light, with some small bid lists circulating.
Long-term municipals are trading at about 84 percent of long-term Treasuries. "Munis are in good shape if you look at ratios," a municipal analyst said.

As for Election Day, about $15 billion of bond issues are on the ballot. The largest bond issues can be found in California, New York and North Carolina, which account for more than half of the dollar volume on the ballot.
Primary market activity will be light for Tuesday, with $90.7 million of issues in 10 offerings slated for sale.
The competitive sector features six issues totaling $71 million, with a $35 milion University of Texas Regents issue topping the slate.
In the negotiated sector, $19.7 million of issues in four offerings are slated for sale.

An additional eight negotiated deals totaling $486 million are on Reuter's day-to-day calendar for Tuesday November 5, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues depending on market conditions. A $255 million California Department of Water Resources offering through Goldman Sachs & Co tops the possible sales slate.

The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade closed at 116-6/32, up on the day, while the December U.S. Treasury futures was at 113. As a result, the MOB spread stood at 102 ticks.
